title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - streaming stability, tool/function-calls, roles/stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Ava Chen
description:
This PR completes parity work for the OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer covering: streaming stability for chunked events, function/tool-calling semantics during streaming, role handling and stop token semantics, inclusion of token-level logprobs in non-streaming and streaming paths, and response formatting/structured output alignment with expected OpenAI shapes. Context: downstream customers expect nearly drop-in compatibility for chat completions (roles, stops, function call hints, streaming event order, and logprobs). Previous iterations handled basic payloads but had mismatches in: (1) streaming event ordering for function calls, (2) stop token clipping across batches, (3) omission of token logprobs in some streaming fallbacks, and (4) subtle differences in content/role normalization that affected structured output parsing. Changes in this PR are limited to the compatibility shim and protocol adapters; no runtime kernel changes. Key commitments: - Maintain existing Redwood runtime performance and SLOs. - Expose the same fields/ordering as OpenAI for both streaming and non-streaming clients. - Add an integration test matrix against the OpenAI-compat test harness (roles, stop positions, logprobs, function-call stream interleaving). The description below captures the main behavioral changes and rationale.

Behavioral changes and rationale:
1) Streaming event framing: introduce deterministic ordering for events emitted during function/tool calls. We now emit: delta content chunks -> delta function_call.name/arguments (when partial) -> done event with final role and function_call.complete payload. This addresses client-side parsers that assumed a single-streamed function call event.
2) Function/tool calling: support partial function_call.arguments streamed as separate deltas and ensure the final function_call payload is present on the final done event. This matches OpenAI's chunking and fixes truncation seen in long-argument tool outputs.
3) Roles normalization: messages supplied without explicit "assistant" role are normalized but preserved in metadata so downstream structured-output validators still receive expected role fields.
4) Stop semantics: stop token clipping has been corrected to operate at the granularity of the stitched output across batches; we now ensure stop tokens are removed exactly once and position offsets in logprobs reflect the clipped content.
5) Logprobs: token-level logprob arrays are now populated for both streaming deltas (when available) and final aggregated responses. For streaming we emit partial logprobs with clear offsets; clients that cannot consume streaming logprobs will still receive the full logprobs in the final response.
6) Response formatting: structured output (json_schema / discriminator handling) is preserved; we added a formatting pass in the compatibility layer that mirrors OpenAI spacing/newline behaviors that some SDKs rely on.

Backwards compatibility: This is non-breaking for Redwood API consumers but changes the compat-layer output ordering and extra fields to match OpenAI. Existing Redwood-only clients are unaffected.

Tests and validation: - Unit tests for message normalization, stop clipping, and logprob offsets. - End-to-end streaming integration tests exercising function_call chunking and interleaved logprob emission. - Cross-compat harness that asserts parity with the reference OpenAI-compat fixtures (stored in eval-harness).

Linear/Jira: ENG-4521 (primary), ENG-4580 (streaming robustness), SUP-1120 (customer incident that motivated fix).

Rollout plan: feature gated behind an opt-in compatibility flag for one release, then enabled by default after two weeks of telemetry.

Observability: added metrics for "compat.streaming.events_per_response" and a tagging dimension "compat_mode=openai_chat_completions" to help detect regressions.
commits_summary: Split into 5 commits: 1) openai_compat: add streaming event orchestrator and ordering tests; 2) openai_compat: implement partial function_call arguments emission; 3) normalization: role/stop/logprob adjustments; 4) sdk: python/ts compatibility helpers and examples; 5) tests: integration fixtures and CI matrix entries.
review_comments: Diego Morales: Can you add a short explanation for why partial function_call.arguments are emitted as deltas rather than buffered? Concerned about memory for very large arguments.

Ava Chen: We buffer up to a configurable soft limit (10MB) then stream; added comment and config option (compat.max_function_argument_buffer_bytes) with sensible default. Memory-constrained Dedicated customers can tune this.
Priya Nair: Tests look good — please add an assertion for final logprob length matching aggregated token count.
Ava Chen: Added assertion and corner-case test for stop at token boundary; CI green locally.
Samir Kapoor: Approved — verified integration fixture against reference harness and found no diffs in event ordering or final json shape.
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity for streaming function/tool calls, roles, stop handling, and token-level logprobs; opt-in compatibility flag for one release. See docs/openai_compat.md for migration notes.
